physicalNotes: Radius 0.19181015 Jupiter radii from Crossfield et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..226....7C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract): 13,712.9 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0166 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Crossfield et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..226....7C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL__2016): P 6.98541 d
sources.shape: Crossfield et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..226....7C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL__2016): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.0559 au and stellar radius 0.426 solar radii; Vanderburg et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..222...14V), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname VANDERBURG_ET_AL__2016): inclination derived from its impact parameter 0.88 with the orbit's a/R* 28.2167 (Winn 2010, eq. 7)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Crossfield et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..226....7C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL__2016): transit mid-time 2456987.3785 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 626 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
